questions_and_answers.question_text: What spelling change begins in the Money Module?
After which letters will the umlaut still be written?
Which counter is used for soap, and what does it literally mean?
What is the literal meaning of dàren?
What is the literal meaning of xiǎoháizi?
How is the letter u pronounced after j, q, x, and y?

answers.answer_text: As if it were written ü.

questions_and_answers.question_text: How would júzi have been written in earlier modules?
Write the Chinese for "He has come to do business."
Write the Chinese for "He is already an adult."
Which expression for "child" is more commonly used than háizi?

articles.text:
Notes on Additional Required Vocabulary

12. júzi                oranges, tangerines
13. píjiǔ               beer
14. yíkuài féizào       one bar of soap
15. zuò mǎimai          to do business
16. dàren               adult
17. xiǎoháizi           child

Júzi: In earlier modules, this word would have been written jǘzi. Starting in the Money Module, the umlaut (¨) will be written only after the n and l, following the normal spelling rule in Pinyin romanization. You will have to remember that the letter u after j, q, x, and y is pronounced as if it were written ü.

Yíkuài féizào: The counter used for soap is -kuài. It literally means "a lump" but is also translated as "a piece."

Zuò mǎimai, "to do business/trade"

Tā lái zuò mǎimai le.            He has come to do business.

Dàren, "adult," literally, "big person"

Tā yǐjing shi dàren le.          He is already an adult.

Xiǎoháizi: Although háizi means "child," the expression more commonly used is xiǎoháizi, literally, "small child."
